'''''Salvia guaranitica''''', the '''anise-scented sage''' or '''hummingbird sage''', is a species of flowering plant in the sage family, ''Lamiaceae'', native to a wide area of [[South America]], including [[Brazil]], [[Paraguay]], [[Uruguay]], and [[Argentina]]. It is cultivated all over the world, and is [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in [[New Zealand]] and [[Chile]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.4067/S0717-66432021000100095|title= ''Salvia guaranitica'' A. St.-Hil. Ex Benth. (Lamiaceae): A new record for the alien flora of Chile|year= 2021|last1= Santa Cruz|first1= Javier|last2= González|first2= Diego|last3= Valdebenito|first3= Samuel|last4= Peñaloza|first4= Patricia|journal= Gayana. Botánica|volume= 78|pages= 95–98|s2cid= 244611065|doi-access= free}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a perennial [[subshrub]] growing {{convert|4|to|5|ft|m|abbr=on}} tall, spreading into a large patch via its spreading roots. The leaves are [[Glossary of leaf morphology#ovate|ovate]], {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and nearly as wide, with a fresh mint green color, and an anise scent when crushed. The [[inflorescence]]s are up to {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on}} long with flowers in various shades of blue, including an uncommonly true blue. In cold regions, flowering begins in mid summer and continues until frost.<ref name="Clebsch">{{cite book|last1=Clebsch|first1=Betsy|last2=Barner|first2=Carol D.|title=The New Book of Salvias|publisher=Timber Press|year=2003|page=140|isbn=978-0-88192-560-9|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NM0iwB8GrQYC&pg=PA140}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Salvia guaranitica Black ^ Blue - Flickr - peganum.jpg|thumb|left|'Black and Blue' cultivar]]
''Salvia guaranitica'' is a popular [[ornamental plant]] in mild areas. It grows in either full or three quarter sunlight, in well-draining soil. Numerous [[cultivar]]s have been selected, including 'Argentine Skies' (pale blue flowers), 'Black and Blue' (very dark violet blue calyx), 'Blue Ensign' (large blue flowers), and 'Purple Splendor' (Light purple flowers).<ref name="Clebsch" /> 

The cultivar 'Blue Enigma', with pure blue flowers, has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Salvia guaranitica'' 'Blue Enigma'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/65598/Salvia-guaranitica-Blue-Enigma/Details | access-date = 17 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 95 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 October 2018}}</ref>

The species name originates from the [[Guaraní people]] of Brazil, who reportedly used the leaves as a sedative.<ref>{{cite book
| editor-first = Yashwant Vishnupant| editor-last = Pathak| title = Handbook of Nutraceuticals Volume I: Ingredients, Formulations, and Applications| publisher = [[CRC Press]]| edition = | date = 24 November 2009| location = | page = 301 |url = https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Handbook_of_Nutraceuticals_Volume_I/dRa-TtRsXSkC&pg=PA301
| isbn = 9781420082227 }}</ref>
